newsitem.title: UK: LIFFE coffee claws back some ground but ends weakeR.
newsitem.headline: LIFFE coffee claws back some ground but ends weakeR.

text.p: Robusta coffee futures largely reflectedsentiment swings in New York on Monday but the London market's overall tone stayed bearish and pressured by origin selling, traders said.
Activity in London was generally described as subdued and traders said the day's price movements had to be viewed in the background of thin turnover.
"There's been some origin (selling) but it's very thin," said one.
After a weak morning session, London fell further after September arabicas broke through initial 175.00 cents/lb support.
But it then struggled to push higher as commercial buying and local shortcovering boosted prices in New York. September hit a high of 185.00, up 5.50 on the day.
At the close September was down $15 at $1,845 after moving in a range of $62. Spot July was down $15 at $1,825 and volume reached 2,736 lots.
The only fresh fundamental news cited by traders concerned the latest private forecast of Brazil's 1997/98 crop by Leon Yallouz, former agronomist for the U.S. Agriculture Department.

Brazilian traders said they believed Yallouz had estimated a crop of around 28 million 60-kg bags, higher than the previous forecast. But other traders said they had heard the figure was 28.6 million bags.
Yallouz' previous forecast at the end of February was said to have been for 27.5 million bags although this has never been confirmed.
